explanation: One proven provenance correction is needed at kim-zubarev-primary-source-intake.json:71 and acquisition-complete-agent-report.json:48: the saved publisher browser DOM contains the loaded book and chapter table of contents marked “No Access,” not a persistent security-verification page. Read-only audits verified all 47 new artifact byte counts/SHA256/MD5 records, the retained archive PDF/TXT hashes, all 41 retrieval-receipt hashes, the report’s intake hash, complete 15-page arXiv and six-page journal extractions with sequential printed journal pages, seven-page archive coverage, DOI/title/author/date metadata and saved-image readability; blank archival Eq(11), edition distinctions and failure-body qualifications remain honestly preserved. Missing exact 2006 chapter bytes are an explicitly authorized limitation—not a campaign-wide access blocker—and mirror-sourced APS typesetting is not direct publisher authentication; saved records provide no evidence of prohibited interactions, although they do not independently reconstruct all historical browser activity.

findings.title: Record the loaded publisher landing instead of a security blocker
findings.body: The saved `kim-mixtures-publisher-security.dom.html` contradicts this final access classification: line 22 is titled `Condensed Matter Nuclear Science`, and line 2299 contains the publisher's table of contents, including the exact `_0058` chapter title, both authors, pp. 711–717 and a `No Access` badge. The 15:20:24 DOM receipt therefore preserves a successfully loaded publisher landing, not a page remaining at “Performing security verification”; the same stale claim appears in `acquisition-complete-agent-report.json:48`. Replace both statements with the observed distinction—direct chapter-PDF HTTP403, browser book landing loaded and chapter marked No Access—and retain the absent publisher fulltext as a documented limitation, without inferring chapter-byte authentication or security-check interaction.
